question: Does equal-sensor evidence weighting reduce dense-sensor consensus errors without changing freshness or candidate agreement gates?
hypothesis: Point-count dominance can choose moving-target consensus; equal sensor mass and stratified proposals reduce that bias. Scene ambiguity remains possible.

estimator.proposal: sample 3 different sensor IDs uniformly, then one detection uniformly per ID
estimator.score: mean inlier fraction across all observed sensors; tie lower weighted inlier residual
estimator.fit: weighted least squares, each sensor has equal total mass before masking

attack_semantics: Compromised authorized CAN candidate and peer sign fresh reports; preserve yaw,steering,acceleration; radar-match assumes attacker knows available radar estimate. No alteration of radar.
offline_INS: scoring only; no estimation, fitting, attack crafting or parameter selection
stopping_rule: One frozen candidate, report all outcomes; do not tune after seeing results.
